# Phase 6 consolidated third-party approval request

Generated 2026-09-08. Required by D3 obligation 6, which says each phase produces
one consolidated request rather than a stream of individual asks. No such file existed.

D3 obligation 3 is the reason this matters, and it is the rule D3 calls the single
most important in the file:

> "It was already published on the live site" is not approval. Existing live project
> pages naming third parties are treated as unapproved until a row exists.

`project-approvals.csv` held a header and nothing else. It now holds 40 rows,
every one UNAPPROVED, covering 5,193 page-occurrences.

## How to work through this

Mark `status` APPROVED and fill `approved_by` and `approved_date`. Anything left
UNAPPROVED gets the D3 obligation 5 treatment: an accurate generic descriptor in place
of the name, never an invented one.

## General contractors named as clients (6)

These carry the most risk. D3 flags questionnaire item 55, subcontract publicity
clauses, as still open. A subcontract that forbids publicising the relationship makes
naming the GC a contract issue, not a marketing preference.

**Verdex needs deciding first and not on marketing grounds.** It is the GC on Panther
National and the counterparty in the active $311K dispute. See PC-17.

## Manufacturer relationships (9)

Lowest risk of the three. ACG can attest to being an installer for a line it installs.
Worth confirming anyway that each manufacturer is content to be named that way, since
several allow it only for certified or authorised dealers.
